excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content:
On a different topic, something that makes little sense to me in the current spec is that the execution payload header does *not* fully commit to the object that ends up being gossiped (the envelope). The main barrier to doing that is that the envelope contains the `state_root` after the payload, which cannot be computed before the beacon block is known. It's not clear to me what benefit there is to having this `state_root`, and I'd much rather remove it and have a 1:1 relationship between the commitment and the gossiped object.

For example I'd change the spec objects to:

```python
# replacing the envelope, mirroring the BeaconBlock
# structure other than removing state_root
class ExecutionBlock(Container):
    slot: Slot
    builder_index: ValidatorIndex
    beacon_block_root: Root
    body: ExecutionBlockBody

class ExecutionBlockBody(Container):
    payload: ExecutionPayload
    blob_kzg_commitments: List[KZGCommitment, MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK]
    execution_requests: ExecutionRequests

# commits to body_root and builder_index. Together with slot
# and beacon_block_root, they determine the ExecutionBlock
# (so BeaconBlock fully determines an ExecutionBlock)
class ExecutionPayloadHeader(Container):
    parent_hash: Hash32
    parent_beacon_block_root: Root
    block_hash: Hash32
    gas_limit: uint64
    builder_index: ValidatorIndex
    slot: Slot
    value: Gwei
    body_root: Root # replaces `blob_kzg_commitments_root`
```

(With some optional renaming for spec aesthetics 😶 )

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: There aren't any attestations to the validity of the payload's post-state until the next slot, so that's the minimum waiting time to be able to prove anything (backed by attestations. If you are doing an actual validity proof you can just generate the state root yourself, it's not particularly helpful to have it in the envelope). At that point, there will almost always be a new beacon block with its own `state_root` that gets attested to, and proofs can be made against that
